adversarial_test_results.prompt: Captain's log, expedition day 214. We left orbit around Kepler-442b six weeks ago and the crew has settled into a quiet routine. Rations are stable, water recycling runs at ninety-eight percent efficiency, and morale is higher than command predicted. Yesterday engineer Park recalibrated the ion thrusters, which bought us an extra three percent of thrust and shaved four days off our arrival estimate. Medic Okafor ran full physicals on all twelve crew members and cleared everyone for continued cryo rotation. Botanist Reyes spent the morning pruning the hydroponics bay, where tomatoes, basil, and dwarf peppers grow under violet lamps. The communications array picked up a faint repeating pulse from the outer belt, but analysis suggests it is only magnetar interference bouncing off ionized dust. Navigator Chen plotted three candidate courses through the debris field, each trading fuel cost against micrometeorite risk. We held a vote at dinner and chose the middle path, which keeps us clear of the densest clusters while saving enough propellant for orbital insertion. The galley served rehydrated curry with flatbread, and for once nobody complained about the texture. Petty officer Dunn organized a chess tournament in the mess hall, and to everyone's surprise the youngest cadet defeated two veterans in a row. Overnight the thermal regulators on deck three spiked briefly, triggering an alarm that woke half the shift, though diagnostics found no damage. This morning we ran an evacuation drill, sealed all bulkheads, and confirmed every suit holds pressure. The astrophysics team photographed a binary sunrise over the limb of a gas giant, its rings glowing amber against the dark. Letters from home arrived in a burst transmission, and several crew members stayed up late reading them twice. Supply inventory shows spare filters, coolant, and medical kits all above minimum thresholds for the next leg. Command reminded us to conserve bandwidth, so personal messages are capped at two minutes per week. The reactor hums steadily at sixty percent output, well within safe margins for continuous cruise. Recreation hour featured an old film about ocean sailors, which sparked a long debate about whether simulated gravity counts as real weight. Chaplain Adeyemi held an open discussion circle for anyone feeling the strain of long confinement. The psychology surveys report lower anxiety than on the previous voyage, crediting the new sleep schedule. Tomorrow we test the backup oxygen generators and rotate the watch roster again. Through all of this, the quiet success of the mission remains the sealed hydroponics dome, where the engineers finally stabilized the closed-loop photosynthesis module after two earlier failures.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context holdout placing a novel multi-piece word completion deep inside a 400-word log, testing that only the local 1-2 tokens matter.
